query: For a high-entropy alloy designed as a single-phase solid solution and exhibiting a favorable strength–ductility combination, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to preserve toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading? Explain the hypothesized mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the same alloy tested under identical conditions without the intervention, define the applicable exposure and loading regime, identify supporting evidence from prior observations, and specify an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of molybdenum (Mo) to a high-entropy alloy (HEA) preserves toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading by preventing phase segregation and maintaining solid solution strengthening.
generation.conditions: Thermal exposure at 700°C and subsequent loading
generation.structural_mediator: Solid solution strengthening and prevention of phase segregation
generation.mechanism: Mo addition prevents depletion of solute interstitials, maintaining solid solution strengthening and preventing phase segregation, which leads to preservation of toughness
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved toughness after thermal exposure and subsequent loading compared to the same alloy without Mo addition
generation.boundary: Thermal exposure at 700°C and subsequent loading
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of Mo required for optimal toughness preservation and the potential effects of other alloying elements on the mechanism

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the toughness of HEAs with and without Mo addition after thermal exposure at 700°C and subsequent loading
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the toughness of the HEA with Mo addition is not significantly improved compared to the same alloy without Mo addition, the hypothesis is falsified
